questions.text: This section is taken from which gland?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The parotid gland is purely serous, characterized by closely packed round serous acini with dark basophilic basal cytoplasm (RER) and apical eosinophilic zymogen granules, prominent striated ducts, and intervening adipocytes, with NO mucous acini.
questions.keyConcept: Parotid gland: Purely serous acini with prominent striated and intercalated ducts, no mucous units.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The red (vermilion) margin of the lip is a transitional zone covered by thin, non-keratinized or lightly keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with high, vascular dermal connective tissue papillae close to the surface, lacking sweat and sebaceous glands.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Striated ducts are lined by simple columnar epithelium with centrally placed spherical nuclei, intensely eosinophilic cytoplasm, and distinct basal vertical striations corresponding to deep basal plasma membrane infoldings packed with vertically oriented elongated mitochondria for active electrolyte reabsorption (Na+) and secretion (K+, HCO3-).

questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana (dwarf tapeworm) is the only human cestode capable of internal autoinfection: eggs released in the small intestine can hatch prematurely without exiting the body. The released hexacanth oncospheres penetrate the intestinal villi, develop into cysticercoids, and re-emerge into the lumen to mature into adult worms, perpetuating heavy worm burdens.

Option A is incorrect because hydatid cyst protoscolices develop into adults only in canine definitive hosts. Option C is incorrect because T. saginata does not cause human cysticercosis or autoinfection.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana: Only cestode with internal autoinfection (eggs hatch in lumen, cysticercoids in villi).

questions.text: Structure 2 in this specimen is composed of:
options: Numerous follicular testes scattered in the body
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: The male Schistosoma mansoni possesses 6 to 9 testes arranged in a compact zigzag cluster situated dorsally near the anterior end behind the ventral sucker. In contrast, S. haematobium has 4 to 5 testes in a straight line.

Option A describes female flukes. Option C describes cestodes. Option E describes Fasciola (two deeply branched testes).
questions.keyConcept: Male Schistosoma mansoni is characterized by 6–9 testes clustered behind the ventral sucker.

questions.text: A carrier of an adult tapeworm developed cysticercosis through autoinfection. Which figure shows the gravid segment of his worm?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Human cysticercosis occurs exclusively with Taenia solium (the pork tapeworm), never Taenia saginata. A patient harboring an adult T. solium can develop cysticercosis through external autoinfection (fecal-oral ingestion of gravid eggs) or internal autoinfection (reverse peristalsis carrying gravid segments into the stomach, where gastric acid digests the egg shell).
questions.keyConcept: Taenia solium causes human cysticercosis via autoinfection; T. saginata does not.

questions.text: Rectal prolapse is a complication of heavy infection with this worm. Interpret.
options: Chronic blood loss causes atrophy of the anal sphincter
Gravid females migrate out at night, causing straining during sleep
A bolus of entangled adult worms obstructs the rectum and pushes it outwards
Flask-shaped ulcers weaken the rectal wall
The worm is deeply embedded in the mucosa by its thin anterior part, causing loss of muscle tone in heavy infection
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Rectal prolapse is a hallmark complication of heavy Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) infection (Trichuris Dysentery Syndrome) in malnourished children. Thousands of adult worms embed their thread-like anterior ends into the cecal and rectal mucosa, causing intense inflammation, tenesmus, and chronic straining that precipitates rectal prolapse.
questions.keyConcept: Heavy Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) infection causes rectal prolapse in children due to severe tenesmus.

questions.text: Identify the station and its identifying criterion:
options: Entamoeba coli cyst - up to 8 nuclei with eccentric karyosomes
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - 1-4 nuclei with central karyosomes
Giardia lamblia cyst - 4 nuclei and axostyles
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - up to 8 nuclei with central karyosomes
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The mature cyst of Entamoeba histolytica measures 10–15 µm, contains 1 to 4 vesicular nuclei with fine, centrally placed karyosomes and evenly distributed peripheral chromatin, and often displays rod-shaped chromatoid bars with rounded ends. Entamoeba coli cysts contain up to 8 nuclei with eccentric karyosomes.
questions.keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica cyst: 1–4 nuclei, small central karyosome, rounded chromatoid bodies.

questions.text: Identify the station and its relevance to man:
options: Cysticercus bovis - it causes human cysticercosis after eating the eggs
Hydatid cyst - man is an accidental intermediate host
Cysticercoid of H. nana - it develops in the human intestinal villi
Cysticercus cellulosae - it can develop in the human brain
Cysticercus bovis - man is infected by eating it in undercooked beef, but it does not develop in man
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hydatid disease (cystic echinococcosis) is caused by the larval stage of Echinococcus granulosus. Dogs and canids are the definitive hosts harboring adult worms; sheep and herbivores are natural intermediate hosts. Humans become accidental intermediate hosts by ingesting eggs passed in dog feces.
questions.keyConcept: Echinococcus granulosus: Humans are accidental dead-end intermediate hosts harboring hydatid cysts.

questions.text: This parasite may cause megaloblastic anemia. Interpret.
options: The adult worm sucks blood from the intestinal mucosa
The adult worm in the small intestine takes up large amounts of dietary vitamin B12
The eggs embolize to the bone marrow
Larvae invade the stomach and destroy the parietal cells
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Diphyllobothrium latum (the broad fish tapeworm) resides in the ileum and actively absorbs massive quantities of host dietary vitamin B12 (up to 80–100%), depriving the human host and producing megaloblastic / pernicious-like anemia with subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.
questions.keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum causes megaloblastic anemia by competing for dietary vitamin B12 in the ileum.

questions.text: All of the following eggs are mature EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola and Ascaris eggs are passed unembryonated (immature) in fresh stool, requiring external development in water or moist soil before becoming infective. In contrast, Enterobius and Heterophyes eggs are passed fully embryonated (mature).
questions.keyConcept: Fasciola, Ascaris, and Hookworm eggs are passed immature (unsegmented) in stool.

questions.text: Food handlers are a serious source of this infection. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the infection is transmitted only through water
No - the cyst must mature in soil before it becomes infective
Yes - asymptomatic carriers pass mature quadrinucleate cysts that are infective on passage and contaminate food
Yes - trophozoites survive on food and invade the colon
No - only trophozoites are passed, and they die quickly outside the body
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cysts of Entamoeba histolytica and Giardia lamblia are immediately infective upon excretion and are resistant to environmental chlorination. Chronic carriers working as food handlers readily transmit cysts to food or beverages via contaminated, unwashed hands.
questions.keyConcept: Entamoeba and Giardia cysts are directly infective upon passage, making food handlers key vectors.

questions.text: Structure 3 in this specimen is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The gynecophoric canal is the deep longitudinal ventral groove formed by the folded lateral margins of the male Schistosoma worm, in which the slender female fluke is embraced during copulation and egg laying.
questions.keyConcept: Schistosoma male: Gynecophoric canal embraces the slender female during copulation.

questions.text: This patient was admitted with diarrhea and abdominal pain. His skin had a diffuse, rapidly moving, erythematous reticular rash from the anal margin to the upper legs. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Trophozoites of Giardia lamblia colonize the duodenal and jejunal brush border, causing malabsorption, foul-smelling steatorrhea, and epigastric cramping without mucosal ulceration or blood.
questions.keyConcept: Giardia lamblia: Duodenal colonization causes watery/fatty non-bloody diarrhea and malabsorption.

questions.text: Identify the station and the main reservoir of infection:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Balantidium coli is the largest protozoan and the only pathogenic ciliate infecting humans. Domestic pigs serve as the primary animal reservoir. Human infection occurs via ingestion of large cysts contaminating water or vegetables in pig-farming areas.
questions.keyConcept: Balantidium coli: Giant ciliated protozoan; pigs are the main natural reservoir host.

questions.text: A 31-year-old HIV-infected woman presents with severe watery diarrhea and dizziness. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cryptosporidium parvum is an opportunistic apicomplexan protozoan causing chronic, life-threatening, cholera-like watery diarrhea and severe dehydration in immunocompromised patients (especially HIV with CD4 < 100/µL). Diagnosis is made by identifying 4–5 µm acid-fast spherical oocysts.
questions.keyConcept: Cryptosporidium parvum causes chronic intractable watery diarrhea in immunocompromised / HIV patients.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) eggs are characteristically planoconvex (flattened on one side and convex on the other, 'D-shaped'), measuring 50–60 × 20–30 µm, possessing a smooth double-contoured translucent shell containing a fully formed tadpole-like coiled larva.
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis egg: D-shaped (planoconvex), colorless translucent shell with coiled larva.

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Taenia spp. mature segment - bilobed ovary
Taenia saginata gravid segment - central uterine stem
Taenia solium gravid segment - lateral uterine branches
Diphyllobothrium latum mature segment - rosette-shaped uterus
Diphyllobothrium latum mature segment - bilobed ovary
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In mature proglottids of Taenia, the female reproductive organs are dominated by a prominent bilobed ovary situated in the posterior third of the segment, along with numerous follicular testes scattered throughout and a lateral genital pore.
questions.keyConcept: Taenia mature segment: Bilobed ovary, median tubular uterus, and scattered follicular testes.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gravid proglottids of Taenia saginata are distinguished from Taenia solium by counting the primary lateral uterine branches on each side of the central stem: T. saginata has 15 to 30 branches (dichotomous branching), whereas T. solium has only 7 to 12 branches (dendritic branching).
questions.keyConcept: Taenia saginata gravid segment: 15–30 main lateral uterine branches on each side.

questions.text: A child presents with appendicitis. Which of the following parasites can cause it?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Adult Enterobius vermicularis pinworms frequently inhabit the cecum and vermiform appendix. In children presenting with symptoms of acute or subacute appendicitis, pinworms in the appendiceal lumen can cause mechanical obstruction or mucosal pin-prick lesions mimicking appendicitis.
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis is the most common helminth discovered inside surgical appendectomy specimens.

questions.text: An Egyptian farmer presented with hematemesis, hepatosplenomegaly and ascites. Sonography showed severe periportal fibrosis. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination during the acute stage?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Schistosoma mansoni adult worms reside in the inferior mesenteric veins. Embolized eggs lodge in the periportal hepatic venules, triggering granulomatous inflammation, Symmers' clay-pipe-stem fibrosis, non-cirrhotic presinusoidal portal hypertension, splenomegaly, and bleeding esophageal varices (hematemesis).
questions.keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni causes Symmers' clay-pipe-stem portal fibrosis, splenomegaly, and esophageal varices.

options: Balantidium coli cyst invading the mucosa
Cryptosporidium parvum stages on the brush border
Balantidium coli trophozoite at the brush border
Balantidium coli cyst at the brush border
Balantidium coli trophozoites invading the mucosa
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cryptosporidium parvum occupies an intracellular but extracytoplasmic position directly within the brush border of intestinal epithelial enterocytes, enclosed in a host-derived parasitophorous vacuole that blunts microvilli and impairs absorption.
questions.keyConcept: Cryptosporidium parvum lives intracellularly but extracytoplasmically on the enterocyte brush border.

questions.text: The structure indicated by the upper arrow is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ancylostoma duodenale possesses a large chitinous buccal capsule equipped on its ventral margin with two pairs of curved pointed teeth, used to lacerate mucosal villi and ingest blood from the small intestinal mucosa.
questions.keyConcept: Ancylostoma duodenale buccal capsule contains two pairs of sharp ventral teeth.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Furcocercous (forked-tail) cercariae of Schistosoma mansoni emerge directly from the freshwater snail Biomphalaria alexandrina (discoidal flat snail) and actively penetrate human intact skin in canal water.
questions.keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni forked-tail cercariae emerge from the intermediate snail Biomphalaria alexandrina.

questions.text: Which of the following eggs is passed mature?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis and Heterophyes heterophyes eggs are passed fully mature (containing a fully developed larva or miracidium) and are immediately infective.
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius and Heterophyes eggs are passed mature (containing fully developed embryos).

questions.text: Chronic blood loss in this infection is multifactorial. Interpret.
options: The worm competes with the host for vitamin B12 and folate in the jejunum
The worm sucks blood, and leaving bleeding points
Larvae damage the lung capillaries, causing repeated hemoptysis
Larvae migrate through the liver, causing bleeding esophageal varices
The worm secretes a hemolysin that lyses red cells inside the portal vessels
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hookworms cause microcytic hypochromic iron-deficiency anemia through two synergistic mechanisms: direct ingestion of blood by the worm (0.15–0.2 mL/day per worm) and persistent capillary oozing from mucosal bite sites due to secreted anticoagulant (acetylcholinesterase and calreticulin).
questions.keyConcept: Hookworm anemia: Mechanical villous laceration, active blood ingestion, and anticoagulant-mediated oozing.

questions.text: Identify the station and the feature that identifies it:
options: Trichocephalus trichiurus in the appendix - bacillary band
Enterobius vermicularis in the appendix - double-bulbed esophagus seen in section
Enterobius vermicularis in the appendix - lateral cuticular alae
Ascaris lumbricoides in the appendix - thick cuticle
Strongyloides stercoralis in the mucosa - eggs in the uterus
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: On histological transverse sections of the appendix, Enterobius vermicularis is definitively identified by two diagnostic lateral cuticular alae (cristae) extending along the body and a muscular double-bulbed esophagus (corpus, isthmus, and spherical posterior bulb).
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis in appendix section: Bilateral pointed cuticular alae and double-bulbed esophagus.

questions.text: Perianal swabbing is the method of choice for diagnosing infection with this egg. Interpret.
options: The eggs are very light and are lost from the surface of the stool sample
The gravid female migrates out of the anus at night and lays her eggs on the perianal skin,
Larvae from these eggs penetrate the perianal skin and stay there
The eggs hatch inside the colon, so only larvae reach the stool
The eggs are digested by colonic bacteria before they are passed
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gravid female Enterobius vermicularis worms migrate out through the anal sphincter at night (when body temperature drops and the host rests) to deposit up to 15,000 sticky eggs on the perianal and perineal skin folds. Because eggs are laid outside the rectum, routine fecal examination is negative in 95% of cases.
questions.keyConcept: Scotch tape test is diagnostic for Enterobius because gravid females oviposit on perianal skin at night.

questions.text: Identify the arrowed stage. Why is it infective as soon as it is passed?
options: Giardia lamblia cyst - it already has 4 nuclei
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - it is mature with 4 nuclei
Cryptosporidium parvum oocyst - it sporulates in the colon after 24 hours
Cryptosporidium parvum oocyst - it is passed already sporulated, containing 4 sporozoites
Cryptosporidium parvum oocyst - it contains 8 merozoites
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The mature infective cyst of Giardia lamblia is oval, measures 8–12 µm, possesses a distinct smooth cyst wall separated from the cytoplasm by a clear space, and contains 4 spherical nuclei along with longitudinal curved axostyles and claw-shaped median bodies.
questions.keyConcept: Giardia lamblia mature cyst: Oval shape, distinct cyst wall, 4 nuclei, and curved central axostyles.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Inside the thick, radially striated, brown embryophore of a Taenia egg lies a spherical hexacanth embryo (oncosphere) bearing 6 chitinous hooklets (3 pairs).
questions.keyConcept: Taenia egg contains a hexacanth embryo (oncosphere) equipped with 6 hooklets.

questions.text: Identify the station and what this stage does after leaving the snail:
options: Leptocercus cercaria of Heterophyes - encysts in fish muscle
Leptocercus cercaria of Fasciola - penetrates human skin
Furcocercus cercaria of Schistosoma - encysts on aquatic plants
Furcocercus cercaria of Schistosoma - penetrates human skin
Leptocercus cercaria of Fasciola - encysts on aquatic plants as a metacercaria
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The lophocercous (pleurocercous) cercaria of Heterophyes heterophyes possesses a dorsal natatory fin-fold. After emerging from Pirenella conica snails, it penetrates and encysts as an infective metacercaria in the flesh of brackish-water fish (Bouri / mullet and Bolti / tilapia).
questions.keyConcept: Heterophyes heterophyes cercaria encysts as infective metacercariae in freshwater/brackish fish.

questions.text: A patient has fever, tenesmus and dysentery. Sigmoidoscopy shows ulcers with a narrow opening, raised edge and wide base. Which figure represents the stage found in the ulcer biopsy?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Acute amoebic dysentery presents with bloody-mucoid stool, lower abdominal cramping, and tenesmus without high toxic fever, demonstrating flask-shaped mucosal ulcers on sigmoidoscopy.
questions.keyConcept: Amoebic dysentery: Stool with blood and mucus, flask-shaped ulcers, trophozoites with ingested RBCs.

questions.text: Growth retardation may be a manifestation of this parasitic infection. Interpret.
options: A bolus of adult worms causes intestinal obstruction
The adult worm absorbs most of the dietary vitamin B12
Autoinfective larvae destroy the intestinal villi
Egg granulomas cause periportal hepatic fibrosis
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In children, heavy Ascaris lumbricoides worm loads contribute to protein-energy malnutrition, vitamin A deficiency, and stunting due to mechanical competition for ingested nutrients and antiprotease enzyme secretion.
questions.keyConcept: Heavy Ascaris burden leads to growth stunting and malnutrition in infected children.

questions.text: Autoinfection is a recognized means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the egg must pass through a snail intermediate host
No - the egg must embryonate in moist soil for 2-3 weeks before it is infective
Yes - the larva inside the egg becomes infective within about 6 hours on the perianal skin, and scratching carries eggs to the mouth
Yes - rhabditiform larvae become filariform larvae inside the intestine
Yes - the egg hatches in the colon and the larva penetrates the colonic wall
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis undergoes external autoinfection (hand-to-mouth via pruritus ani fingernail scratching) because eggs embryonate and become infective within 4–6 hours of oviposition on the warm perianal skin.
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis: Rapid perianal embryonation (4–6 hrs) drives hand-to-mouth autoinfection.

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Anterior end of Enterobius - cephalic ala
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The scolex of Diphyllobothrium latum is elongated and almond-shaped, lacking cup-like suckers and rostellum, characterized instead by two deep longitudinal suction grooves called bothria (one dorsal, one ventral).
questions.keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum scolex: Almond-shaped with two longitudinal sucking grooves (bothria).

questions.text: This parasite causes flask-shaped intestinal ulcers and extra-intestinal manifestations. Interpret.
options: Trophozoites lyse the mucosa with proteolytic enzymes, spread laterally in the submucosa, and reach the liver through the portal vein
Eggs lodge in the bowel wall and cause granulomas that ulcerate
Adult worms embed their anterior ends deep in the mucosa
Trophozoites burrow with their cilia and invade the lymphatics
Cysts excyst in the submucosa and grow into large colonies
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites adhere to colonic mucin via Gal/GalNAc lectin, secrete pore-forming amoebapore and cysteine proteases (histolysin) to lyse epithelial cells, and expand laterally in the loose submucosa, generating classic flask-shaped ulcers.
questions.keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica produces flask-shaped colonic ulcers via cysteine proteases and amoebapore.

questions.text: The middle arrow points to a structure that distinguishes this fluke from Metagonimus yokogawai. It is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The egg of Hymenolepis nana is round to oval, measures 45–50 µm, has two membranes (thin outer shell and thick inner embryophore), and is definitively identified by 4 to 8 hair-like polar filaments originating from mammillated polar thickenings and spreading into the space between membranes.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana egg: Hexacanth embryo with 4–8 wavy polar filaments emerging from polar knobs.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pirenella conica is a small, elongated, turreted conical brackish-water snail inhabiting Northern Egyptian lakes (Manzala, Burullus, Edku) that acts as the essential first intermediate host of Heterophyes heterophyes.
questions.keyConcept: Pirenella conica is the first intermediate snail host of Heterophyes heterophyes in Egyptian lakes.

options: Female of Strongyloides stercoralis with eggs in uterus
Female of Enterobius vermicularis with eggs in uterus
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The scolex of Hymenolepis nana is tiny (0.3 mm), subglobular, featuring 4 cup-like suckers and a single prominent retractable rostellum armed with a single circle of 20 to 30 tuning-fork hooklets.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana scolex: 4 spherical suckers and a retractable rostellum with 20–30 hooklets.

questions.text: Structure 1 in this segment is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The posterior end of the male Ancylostoma duodenale expands into an umbrella-shaped membranous copulatory bursa supported by fleshy rays (1 dorsal, 2 lateral lobes) and two long, slender spicules used during mating.
questions.keyConcept: Male hookworm is identified by its posterior umbrella-shaped copulatory bursa supported by rays.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The egg of Trichuris trichiura is brown, barrel-shaped (lemon-shaped), measures 50 × 22 µm, possesses a thick smooth triple-layered shell, and is characterized by a prominent transparent mucoid plug at each pole.
questions.keyConcept: Trichuris trichiura egg: Barrel-shaped, brown, with clear bipolar mucoid plugs.

questions.text: An abdominal CT of a shepherd with right upper abdominal pain and no fever shows multiple cystic lesions of different sizes in both liver lobes. Which figure represents the stage found when the cyst fluid is examined?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Typical fertilized Ascaris lumbricoides eggs are oval, measure 60–75 × 40–50 µm, enclosed by a thick transparent shell surrounded by a characteristic coarse, golden-brown, bile-stained mamillated albuminous outer coat.
questions.keyConcept: Ascaris lumbricoides fertilized egg: Golden-brown, bile-stained, with a coarse mamillated coat.

questions.text: All of the following parasites can cause appendicitis EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The scolex of Taenia saginata (beef tapeworm) is quadrate (1.5–2 mm), equipped with 4 prominent hemispherical suckers, but is completely UNARMED (lacks both a rostellum and hooklets), distinguishing it from T. solium.
questions.keyConcept: Taenia saginata scolex: 4 suckers, unarmed (no rostellum, no hooks).

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Entamoeba histolytica cyst - nucleus with central karyosome
Entamoeba histolytica trophozoite - nucleus with central karyosome
Entamoeba coli trophozoite - nucleus with eccentric karyosome
Entamoeba coli trophozoite - nucleus with central karyosome
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The egg of Schistosoma mansoni is large (115–175 × 45–70 µm), non-operculated, golden-yellow, and features a prominent, sharp, backward-pointing LATERAL spine near the posterior pole, containing a fully formed miracidium.
questions.keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni egg: Large, oval, golden-yellow, with a sharp prominent LATERAL spine.

questions.text: A patient has hepatomegaly and jaundice. Three months ago he had fever, right upper quadrant pain and eosinophilia after eating green salads. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola gigantica is a giant liver fluke measuring 25–75 × 12 mm, characterized by an elongated lanceolate leaf-like body, a small cephalic cone with indistinct shoulders, and extensively branched intestinal caeca and testes.
questions.keyConcept: Fasciola gigantica: Giant leaf-like fluke with cephalic cone, branched caeca, and branched testes.

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Echinococcus granulosus scolex - rostellum with hooks
Taenia saginata scolex - rostellum with hooks
Taenia solium scolex - rostellum with hooks
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The gravid segment of Taenia solium contains a central longitudinal uterine stem giving off only 7 to 12 thick primary lateral branches on each side, which branch dendritically.
questions.keyConcept: Taenia solium gravid segment: 7–12 lateral uterine branches per side (tree-like / dendritic).

questions.text: Finding this egg in a stool sample does NOT identify the species of the infecting worm. Interpret.
options: The egg is passed unembryonated, so the hexacanth embryo cannot be examined
The striated shell is dissolved by stool preservatives before examination
Eggs of T. saginata and T. solium are morphologically identical, so the gravid segment or scolex is needed
The egg is identical to the H. nana egg, which is the commonest cause
Eggs of T. solium are passed only in patients with cysticercosis
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ascaris lumbricoides is the largest intestinal nematode of humans (females 20–35 cm, males 15–30 cm with curved tail), pale pink/creamy white, cylindrical with pointed ends, bearing three sensory lips around the anterior mouth.
questions.keyConcept: Ascaris lumbricoides adult: Giant creamy cylindrical roundworm with three anterior sensory lips.

questions.text: This snail is the first intermediate host of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Lymnaea cailliaudi (Lymnaea natalensis) is a freshwater snail with a conical, dextral spiral shell that serves as the intermediate host of Fasciola hepatica and Fasciola gigantica in Egypt.
questions.keyConcept: Lymnaea cailliaudi: Freshwater dextral conical snail, essential host of Fasciola.

questions.text: A 4-year-old child has pruritus ani, insomnia and nocturnal enuresis. Which figure represents the stage recovered by perianal swab?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Nocturnal perianal pruritus (pruritus ani), restlessness, and sleep disturbances in young children are caused by migrating female Enterobius vermicularis worms discharging eggs onto the perianal skin.
questions.keyConcept: Pruritus ani and sleep disturbance in young children = Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm).

questions.text: A 4-year-old child has diarrhea with pale, loose, offensive, fatty stools and no mucus or blood. Which figure represents the stage found in a fresh diarrheic stool?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pale, frothy, greasy, malodorous diarrhea floating in water (steatorrhea) accompanied by abdominal distension and flatulence is the hallmark of Giardia lamblia duodenitis / malabsorption.
questions.keyConcept: Pale greasy floating diarrhea (steatorrhea) + flatulence = Giardia lamblia trophozoites.

questions.text: All of the following eggs are passed immature EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis eggs are fully embryonated (mature) when deposited, whereas Ascaris, Trichuris, and Fasciola eggs are passed unembryonated (immature).
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius eggs are passed fully mature; Ascaris, Trichuris, and Fasciola eggs are immature.

questions.text: Structure 2 in this segment is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The lateral fields of Fasciola are densely packed with highly branched, granular vitelline follicles extending from the ventral sucker to the posterior tip of the fluke.
questions.keyConcept: Lateral fields of Fasciola are occupied by extensive branched follicular vitelline glands.

questions.text: Finding this egg in a single stool sample does not always mean active infection. Interpret.
options: The egg is a degenerated form that has lost its operculum
The egg is shed only in the acute (invasive) stage of the disease
The egg may pass transiently after eating infected raw liver , so stool is re-examined after a liver-free diet
The egg is shed only in bile, so duodenal aspirate is needed
The egg is identical to the Heterophyes egg, so serology is required
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Finding Fasciola eggs in a single stool sample does not necessarily prove active hepatic infection; it may represent spurious (false) infection following the ingestion of cooked or raw infected sheep or cattle liver containing unabsorbed passing eggs. Re-examination after a 3-day liver-free diet confirms true infection.
questions.keyConcept: Spurious Fasciola infection: Liver ingestion causes false-positive stool eggs; repeat after 3-day liver-free diet.

questions.text: The arrowed structure in this larva is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The rhabditiform larva of nematodes features a characteristic muscular rhabditiform esophagus consisting of an anterior cylindrical corpus, a constricted isthmus, and a swollen posterior bulb.
questions.keyConcept: Rhabditiform larva possesses a muscular esophagus with a posterior spherical bulb.

questions.text: Identify the specimen and the feature indicated by the lower arrow:
options: Strongyloides stercoralis female - tapering posterior end
Trichocephalus trichiurus female - blunt posterior end
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The male hookworm is recognized by its broad, fan-like copulatory bursa supported by rays, contrasting with the simple tapering pointed tail of female worms.
questions.keyConcept: Male hookworm tail features a specialized expanded copulatory bursa.

questions.text: In this cyst aspirate, the arrowed structures are the hooks of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Microscopic examination of clear hydatid fluid reveals 'hydatid sand', comprising thousands of free and brood-capsule-derived invaginated protoscolices, each bearing 4 suckers and a crown of chitinous hooklets.
questions.keyConcept: Hydatid sand consists of invaginated protoscolices and detached hooklets from Echinococcus.

questions.text: A child presents with appendicitis. Which figure represents the diagnostic stage?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cross-section of vermiform appendix revealing cross-sections of Enterobius vermicularis worms with pointed lateral cuticular crests inside the appendiceal lumen.
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis in appendiceal cross-section showing characteristic lateral cuticular crests.

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Immature and mature cysts of Entamoeba histolytica frequently contain cylindrical, rod-like chromatoid bodies with characteristically blunt, rounded, cigar-shaped ends (condensed RNA/ribosomes).
questions.keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica chromatoid bodies have blunt, rounded, cigar-shaped ends.

questions.text: Identify the egg and the source of infection:
options: Heterophyes heterophyes egg - raw or undercooked fish
Fasciola egg - raw or undercooked fish
Heterophyes heterophyes egg - aquatic plants such as watercress
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Heterophyes heterophyes eggs are small (28–30 × 15–17 µm), operculated, yellowish-brown with a light bulb appearance. Human infection results from consuming raw, insufficiently salted, or undercooked brackish-water fish (e.g., Fesikh, mullet, tilapia) containing encysted metacercariae.
questions.keyConcept: Heterophyes heterophyes: Ingestion of raw/pickled brackish fish (Fesikh) containing metacercariae.

questions.text: This parasite can be transmitted to humans by autoinfection. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - this parasite infects only by larval skin penetration
Yes - the egg is infective on passage and is carried from the anus to the mouth
No - the egg can only infect after passing through Cyclops
Yes - the egg hatches in the small intestine and the larva migrates through the lungs again
No - the egg is passed with a one-cell ovum and needs about 2-3 weeks in soil to become embryonated
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Strongyloides stercoralis undergoes internal autoinfection: non-infective rhabditiform larvae in the intestinal lumen can molt into infective filariform larvae before excretion. These filariform larvae immediately penetrate the perianal skin or colonic mucosa, entering the circulation to perpetuate infection for decades.
questions.keyConcept: Strongyloides stercoralis causes internal autoinfection when rhabditiform larvae molt into filariform larvae in the gut.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The egg of Enterobius vermicularis contains a fully developed, coiled, tadpole-like vermiform larva when shed onto perianal skin.
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis egg contains a fully formed mature larva.

questions.text: Structure 2 in this egg is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Structure 2 represents the thick, irregular, tuberculated mamillated albuminous coat secreted by the uterine wall, which stains golden-brown from fecal bile pigments.
questions.keyConcept: Ascaris outer shell: Coarse, uneven, bile-stained mamillated albuminous coat.

questions.text: Layer 1 in this section is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The wall of a hydatid cyst comprises an outer host-derived fibrous capsule (pericyst), a middle thick, milky-white, acellular laminated cuticular layer (ectocyst), and an inner thin, nucleated cellular germinal layer (endocyst) that buds off brood capsules.
questions.keyConcept: Hydatid cyst wall: Outer acellular laminated layer and inner nucleated germinal layer.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The fertilized Ascaris egg contains an unsegmented spherical one-cell ovum surrounded by a clear perivitelline space at each pole.
questions.keyConcept: Fertilized Ascaris egg contains an unsegmented one-cell zygote.

questions.text: This worm came out through the nose of a child after general anesthesia. Which figure represents the stage found on his stool examination?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In high fevers, anesthesia, or anthelmintic irritation, adult Ascaris lumbricoides worms exhibit wandering erratic behavior, migrating retrograde into the stomach, esophagus, and emerging through the mouth or nose, or obstructing the bile duct.
questions.keyConcept: Erratic Ascaris lumbricoides migration causes adult worms to emerge through the mouth or nostrils.

questions.text: Identify the station. Why can man harbor this stage?
options: Cysticercus cellulosae - man can act as an intermediate host
Cysticercus cellulosae - man is infected only by eating undercooked pork
Cysticercus bovis - reverse peristalsis brings gravid segments to the stomach
Hydatid cyst - man swallows eggs from dog feces
Cysticercus bovis - man is the normal intermediate host
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cysticercus cellulosae is the larval stage of Taenia solium. Humans act as accidental intermediate hosts when they ingest T. solium eggs (via contaminated food/water or autoinfection). Oncospheres hatch in the intestine and encyst in the brain (neurocysticercosis), subcutaneous tissues, and eye.
questions.keyConcept: Humans develop cysticercosis by acting as intermediate hosts harboring Cysticercus cellulosae.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scolex of Taenia saginata: Quadrate shape, 4 cup-like muscular suckers, lacks rostellum and hooks (unarmed).
questions.keyConcept: Taenia saginata scolex: 4 muscular suckers, unarmed (no rostellum, no hooklets).

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed part:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The adult Echinococcus granulosus is minute (3–6 mm long) and consists of a pyriform scolex with 4 suckers and a rostellum of hooks, followed by only 3 proglottids: one immature, one mature, and one large gravid segment.
questions.keyConcept: Echinococcus granulosus adult is 3–6 mm long with only 3 segments (immature, mature, gravid).

questions.text: This parasitic stage is the pathogenic stage of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The hydatid cyst (larval stage) is the pathogenic stage responsible for human cystic echinococcosis, forming space-occupying lesions in the liver (70%) and lungs (20%).
questions.keyConcept: Hydatid cyst is the pathogenic stage causing human echinococcosis.

questions.text: This parasitic stage represents the infective stage of a case of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The thick-walled spherical oocyst (4–5 µm) containing 4 naked sporozoites is the infective stage of Cryptosporidium parvum, excreted in feces and resistant to chlorine.
questions.keyConcept: Cryptosporidium infective stage: Thick-walled sporulated oocyst containing 4 sporozoites.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hookworm (Ancylostoma / Necator) eggs are passed in feces at the 4 to 8 cell segmented stage (morula), surrounded by a thin, smooth, colorless shell with a wide clear space.
questions.keyConcept: Hookworm egg is passed at the 4–8 cell segmented morula stage with a wide clear space.

questions.text: Which feature distinguishes this fluke from Fasciola spp.?
options: Separate sexes with a gynecophoric canal
Branched intestinal caeca with a cephalic cone
Simple, unbranched intestinal caeca and no cephalic cone
A genital sucker beside the ventral sucker
A ventral sucker displaced to one side
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Unlike hermaphroditic trematodes like Fasciola (which have flattened leaf-like bodies containing both male and female organs), Schistosomes are unique flukes with separate sexes (dioecious), where the cylindrical female resides within the male's gynecophoric canal.
questions.keyConcept: Schistosomes are dioecious (separate sexes) with male gynecophoric canal; Fasciola is hermaphroditic.

questions.text: Autoinfection is a means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - infection occurs only by skin penetration by filariform larvae
Yes - the egg hatches in the colon and the larvae re-invade the mucosa
No - man is only an accidental host of this worm
No - the egg is passed with an unsegmented ovum and must embryonate in soil before it becomes infective
Yes - the mucoid plugs dissolve on the perianal skin and release infective larvae
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana eggs can hatch inside the intestinal lumen without reaching the outside world; oncospheres penetrate the intestinal villi to form cysticercoids that return to the lumen as adult worms.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana autoinfection: Eggs hatch in lumen, oncospheres develop in mucosal villi.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola eggs are passed unembryonated, containing an unsegmented ovum surrounded by numerous yellowish-brown vitelline/yolk cells, with an indistinct opercular cap at one pole.
questions.keyConcept: Fasciola egg contains an unsegmented ovum surrounded by granular yolk cells with an operculum.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A spherical oncosphere with 6 embryonic hooklets (hexacanth embryo) enclosed in a thick, radially striated brown embryophore.
questions.keyConcept: Taenia egg contains a hexacanth embryo with 6 hooklets inside a striated embryophore.

questions.text: This snail is the intermediate host of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Biomphalaria alexandrina is a freshwater pulmonate snail with a flat, discoidal, planorbid shell that serves as the intermediate host for Schistosoma mansoni in the Nile delta and valley.
questions.keyConcept: Biomphalaria alexandrina: Flat discoidal planorbid snail, host of Schistosoma mansoni.

questions.text: All of the following eggs are passed mature (embryonated) EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola and Ascaris eggs require external incubation in water or soil to develop, whereas Enterobius and Heterophyes eggs are passed fully mature with infective embryos.
questions.keyConcept: Fasciola eggs are passed immature; Enterobius and Heterophyes eggs are passed mature.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: When excreted in feces, the mature Schistosoma mansoni egg contains a fully developed, active, ciliated miracidium equipped with cephalic glands and flame cells, ready to hatch upon contact with fresh water.
questions.keyConcept: Mature Schistosoma mansoni egg contains a fully formed, ciliated miracidium.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ancylostoma and Necator eggs in fresh feces contain an unhatched segmented ovum consisting of 4 to 8 dark blastomeres (morula stage).
questions.keyConcept: Fresh hookworm egg contains a segmented morula of 4–8 blastomeres.

questions.text: Which of these stages can cause internal autoinfection, so that the whole life cycle is completed inside one human host?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana and Strongyloides stercoralis are the two classic parasites capable of true internal autoinfection within the human alimentary canal.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana and Strongyloides stercoralis undergo internal autoinfection in the intestine.

questions.text: A patient has pallor, puffy eyes and swollen feet. Which figure represents the stage that can be detected in his stool?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Severe chronic Ancylostoma duodenale infection leads to severe iron deficiency anemia (pallor, fatigue) and protein-losing enteropathy (hypoalbuminemia causing dependent pedal edema and periorbital puffiness).
questions.keyConcept: Hookworm disease causes severe microcytic anemia, hypoalbuminemia, and periorbital/pedal edema.

questions.text: Identify the station and the type of anemia this parasite causes:
options: Anterior end of Strongyloides female - microcytic hypochromic anemia
Anterior end of Enterobius - normocytic normochromic anemia
Hookworm buccal capsule - microcytic hypochromic anemia
Hookworm buccal capsule - macrocytic megaloblastic anemia
Hookworm copulatory bursa - microcytic hypochromic anemia
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The anterior end of Ancylostoma duodenale features a bent dorsal hook-like neck and a chitinous buccal capsule with 2 pairs of curved teeth that lacerate mucosal vessels, producing severe microcytic hypochromic iron-deficiency anemia.
questions.keyConcept: Ancylostoma duodenale: Ventral teeth in buccal capsule cause severe microcytic hypochromic anemia.

questions.text: Autoinfection is a means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the egg must embryonate in soil for weeks
Yes - the egg is infective when passed and can hatch in the intestine, where the oncosphere develops into a cysticercoid in the villi
Yes - rhabditiform larvae become filariform larvae in the intestine
Yes - the egg needs about 6 hours on the perianal skin before it becomes infective
No - an insect intermediate host is always needed
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: H. nana eggs can hatch in the small bowel; released hexacanth larvae penetrate intestinal villi, transform into cysticercoids, and emerge into the lumen to attach as mature adults.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana: Direct autoinfection via cysticercoid development in intestinal villi.

questions.text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The viable Schistosoma mansoni egg contains a ciliated miracidium with prominent apical papilla and primitive gut.
questions.keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni egg contains an active ciliated miracidium.

questions.text: The snail that harbors the larval stages of this parasite is:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Lymnaea cailliaudi harbors the sporocyst, rediae, and cercarial stages of Fasciola flukes in Egypt.
questions.keyConcept: Lymnaea cailliaudi supports sporocyst, rediae, and cercarial development of Fasciola.

questions.text: Fatal hyperinfection with this parasite can occur in patients on corticosteroids. Interpret.
options: Eggs hatch in the stomach and release thousands of larvae
Larvae encyst in muscles and are released by steroids
Rhabditiform larvae turn into filariform larvae inside the gut and re-invade (autoinfection), so the worm load rises sharply when immunity falls
Adult worms multiply asexually in the liver
Steroids stimulate the female to lay unembryonated eggs
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In immunocompromised patients or those receiving systemic corticosteroids, Strongyloides internal autoinfection accelerates uncontrollably into 'hyperinfection syndrome' and disseminated strongyloidiasis: millions of filariform larvae penetrate the bowel wall and invade the lungs, liver, and brain, carrying enteric Gram-negative bacteria that cause fatal sepsis and meningitis.
questions.keyConcept: Strongyloides hyperinfection: Steroid therapy triggers massive larval dissemination and fatal sepsis.

questions.text: Identify the egg and its arrowed content:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A decorticated fertilized Ascaris egg lacks the rough brown mamillated albuminous coat (lost during passage or preparation), revealing a smooth, thick, transparent shell enclosing a single unsegmented ovum with crescentic spaces at both poles.
questions.keyConcept: Decorticated Ascaris egg: Smooth colorless shell enclosing a single unsegmented ovum.

questions.text: A stool sample was received in your lab from a patient complaining of bloody diarrhea. Macroscopic appearance showed unformed stool with blood and mucus. Microscopic examination of the sample was done and revealed Gram-negative bacilli. What is the next step to identify the causative organism?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: When a Gram-negative bacillus is visualized from a stool specimen causing bloody diarrhea (dysentery), the primary rapid biochemical step to differentiate Enterobacteriaceae (which are strictly oxidase-negative) from other Gram-negative enteric pathogens (such as Vibrio, Campylobacter, or Pseudomonas, which are oxidase-positive) is the oxidase test.

Option A, C, and D (indole, urease, citrate) are secondary biochemical reactions (part of the IMViC and differential panels) carried out only after confirming family placement and isolating pure colonies on differential/selective media.
questions.keyConcept: Oxidase test differentiates oxidase-negative Enterobacteriaceae (Shigella, Salmonella, E. coli) from oxidase-positive bacilli (Vibrio, Campylobacter, Pseudomonas).

media.caption: Gram stain of stool specimen showing Gram-negative bacilli

questions.text: After isolation of the previous stool sample, the following results were obtained: Oxidase negative, TSI showing alkaline slant / acid butt (K/A, red slant / yellow butt) with no gas and no H2S production, Citrate negative, and Motility negative. The causative agent is most likely:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Shigella species are non-motile, non-lactose fermenting Gram-negative bacilli that produce an alkaline slant / acid butt (K/A) on Triple Sugar Iron (TSI) agar without gas formation (glucose fermented without gas) and without H2S production. They are citrate-negative and oxidase-negative. Clinically, Shigella dysenteriae invades the colonic mucosa, producing acute bacillary dysentery characterized by painful cramps, tenesmus, and frequent stools containing blood, pus, and mucus.

Option A and B (ETEC, EHEC) are lactose fermenters (A/A on TSI with gas). Option C (Staph. aureus) is a Gram-positive coccus.
questions.keyConcept: Shigella dysenteriae: Non-motile, non-lactose fermenter, TSI K/A (no gas, no H2S), citrate-negative, causes bacillary dysentery.

media.caption: Biochemical reactions: Oxidase negative, TSI K/A (no gas, no H2S), Citrate negative

questions.text: To trace the source of the previous Shigella infection during an outbreak (epidemiological typing), which of the following can be used?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Colicin typing (bacteriocin typing) is the established phenotypic method utilized for epidemiological source tracing and strain differentiation in outbreaks of Shigella sonnei and Shigella dysenteriae. Colicins are bacteriocins produced by certain bacterial strains that inhibit or kill closely related indicator strains.

Option B (Phage typing) is primarily used for Staphylococcus aureus and Salmonella typhi. Option C (Widal test) is an agglutination test for enteric fever (Salmonella). Option D (Serology) identifies O serogroups (A, B, C, D) but is insufficient alone for fine-scale epidemiological strain tracing.
questions.keyConcept: Colicin typing is the specific bacteriocin typing method used for epidemiological tracing of Shigella outbreaks.

questions.text: If isolation of the previous stool sample from a patient with bloody diarrhea had shown the following results instead: Oxidase negative, TSI showing acid slant / acid butt (A/A, yellow/yellow) with gas production, Indole positive (red ring), and Citrate negative, the causative agent would most likely be:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC, classic serotype O157:H7) produces Shiga toxins (Stx1/Stx2) that cause hemorrhagic colitis (grossly bloody diarrhea) with severe abdominal cramps. Biochemically, as an E. coli strain, it is a lactose fermenter producing an acid slant / acid butt (A/A) with gas on TSI, is indole-positive, and citrate-negative. Because the clinical presentation is bloody diarrhea (hemorrhagic colitis), the diagnosis is EHEC rather than ETEC (which causes watery diarrhea).

Option A (ETEC) causes secretory watery diarrhea without blood. Option C (Staph. aureus) causes food poisoning with vomiting. Option D (Shigella) is a non-lactose fermenter (K/A, no gas).
questions.keyConcept: EHEC (e.g. O157:H7): Causes bloody diarrhea (hemorrhagic colitis), lactose fermenter (TSI A/A + gas), indole-positive, citrate-negative.

media.caption: Biochemical panel: TSI A/A with gas, Indole positive (red ring), Citrate negative

questions.text: The suitable selective and differential culture medium for isolation and screening of Enterohemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC O157:H7) from stool would be:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Sorbitol MacConkey (SMAC) agar is the standard selective and differential medium for EHEC O157:H7. Unlike ~95% of commensal E. coli strains which rapidly ferment sorbitol (forming pink/red colonies), E. coli O157:H7 does not ferment sorbitol within 24 hours, forming distinctive colorless/pale colonies on SMAC.

Option A (DCA) and Option C (SS agar) are selective for Salmonella and Shigella. Option D (TCBS) is selective for Vibrio cholerae.
questions.keyConcept: Sorbitol MacConkey (SMAC) agar: EHEC O157:H7 forms colorless/pale colonies because it is sorbitol-negative (non-sorbitol fermenter).

questions.text: A stool sample was received in your lab from a patient complaining of bloody diarrhea. Macroscopic appearance showed unformed stool with blood and mucus. Microscopic examination of the sample revealed non-motile Gram-negative bacilli. What is your provisional diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: The combination of acute dysentery (stool containing blood, mucus, and inflammatory cells) and microscopic detection of non-motile Gram-negative bacilli is pathognomonic for Shigella dysenteriae (Bacillary dysentery). Shigella lacks flagella and is strictly non-motile.

Option A (ETEC) and Option B (EHEC) are motile peritrichous bacilli, and ETEC produces watery diarrhea. Option C (Staph. aureus) is a Gram-positive coccus.
questions.keyConcept: Non-motile Gram-negative bacilli in bloody diarrhea = Shigella dysenteriae (Bacillary dysentery).

media.caption: Microscopic examination showing non-motile Gram-negative bacilli

questions.text: A stool sample was received in your lab from a patient complaining of bloody diarrhea. Macroscopic appearance showed unformed stool with blood and mucus. Microscopic examination of the sample revealed non-motile Gram-negative bacilli. The next step in isolation would be:
options: Isolate on an enrichment medium "selenite broth" followed by subculture on DCA agar
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Because stool contains overwhelming numbers of normal coliform flora (e.g. commensal E. coli, Klebsiella), isolating pathogens like Shigella or Salmonella requires initial enrichment in a liquid medium such as Selenite F broth (which suppresses coliform growth) followed by subculturing onto selective differential solid media such as Deoxycholate Citrate Agar (DCA) or MacConkey agar.

Option A (Blood agar) is non-selective and will be completely overgrown by coliforms and Proteus swarming. Option B alone misses the critical enrichment step necessary to recover low pathogen counts.
questions.keyConcept: Stool pathogen isolation protocol: Inoculation into enrichment medium (Selenite F broth) followed by selective plating on DCA agar.

questions.text: You are provided with a stool sample from a patient complaining of severe rice-water diarrhea. Direct microscopic examination revealed comma-shaped motile organisms. The organism was isolated and showed yellow colonies on a green agar plate. What is your next biochemical step?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Vibrio cholerae produces large, smooth, yellow colonies on Thiosulfate-Citrate-Bile Salts-Sucrose (TCBS) agar due to sucrose fermentation. The key diagnostic biochemical test to rapidly confirm Vibrio cholerae from suspicious colonies is the oxidase test, which is strongly and immediately POSITIVE (dark purple within 10 seconds).

Option A, C, and D: Indole, urease, and citrate do not distinguish Vibrio from other sucrose fermenters as rapidly or specifically as the oxidase reaction.
questions.keyConcept: Vibrio cholerae is strongly oxidase-positive and ferments sucrose on TCBS agar to form yellow colonies.

media.caption: Gram-negative curved bacilli and yellow sucrose-fermenting colonies on TCBS agar

questions.text: You are provided with a stool sample from a patient complaining of severe rice-water diarrhea. Direct microscopic examination revealed comma-shaped motile organisms. The organism was isolated on TCBS. How can you definitively confirm your diagnosis?
options: Agglutination tests to detect O antigens
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Definitive serological confirmation of Vibrio cholerae is achieved by slide agglutination using polyvalent O1 antiserum and O139 antiserum. Agglutination confirms epidemic/pandemic toxigenic cholera strains (V. cholerae O1 serotypes Ogawa, Inaba, Hikojima, or V. cholerae O139 Bengal).

Option A (Colicin typing) is for Shigella. Option B (Phage typing) is for Staph aureus and Salmonella typhi. Option C (Widal test) is for typhoid fever antibodies.
questions.keyConcept: Definitive confirmation of Vibrio cholerae is performed via slide agglutination using specific O1 and O139 antisera.

media.caption: TCBS agar and microscopy of Vibrio cholerae

questions.text: You are provided with a stool sample from a patient complaining of severe rice-water diarrhea. Direct microscopic examination revealed comma-shaped motile organisms. The organism was isolated and showed yellow colonies on TCBS agar. What is your provisional diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: The classic triad of profuse painless 'rice-water' stool (translucent watery fluid with flecks of mucus and epithelial cells), actively motile comma-shaped Gram-negative rods with darting motility, and yellow sucrose-fermenting colonies on TCBS agar establishes the provisional diagnosis of Vibrio cholerae.

Option A (ETEC) and Option B (EPEC) are straight rods and do not grow as yellow colonies on TCBS. Option C (Staph. aureus) causes food poisoning with prominent vomiting and does not grow on TCBS.
questions.keyConcept: Rice-water diarrhea + comma-shaped motile rods + yellow colonies on TCBS = Vibrio cholerae.

media.caption: Vibrio cholerae morphology and TCBS growth

questions.text: You are provided with a stool sample from a patient complaining of severe rice-water diarrhea. Direct microscopic examination revealed comma-shaped motile organisms. Name the specific enrichment medium used in diagnosis:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Alkaline Peptone Water (APW, pH 8.6) is the specific enrichment broth for Vibrio cholerae. V. cholerae tolerates high alkalinity (pH 8.6–9.0) and multiplies rapidly at the surface pellicle within 6–8 hours, while the high pH strongly suppresses normal intestinal flora.

Option B (Selenite broth) and Option C (Tetrathionate broth) are enrichment media for Salmonella and Shigella. Option D (Plain peptone water) is not sufficiently alkaline to suppress commensals.
questions.keyConcept: Alkaline Peptone Water (APW, pH 8.6) is the gold-standard enrichment fluid medium for Vibrio cholerae.

questions.text: In your lab, you received a stool sample from a patient complaining of watery diarrhea. Macroscopic appearance shows watery stool without blood or mucus. The causative agent was isolated on MacConkey agar showing rose-pink colonies. What is your provisional diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) is the leading bacterial cause of watery traveler's diarrhea (secretory diarrhea without blood or pus). On MacConkey agar, E. coli ferments lactose, producing acidic byproducts that turn the neutral red indicator into distinct rose-pink colonies surrounded by precipitated bile salts.

Option B (EHEC) causes bloody diarrhea (hemorrhagic colitis). Option C (Staph. aureus) causes food poisoning with vomiting and does not grow on MacConkey agar. Option D (Vibrio cholerae) is a non-lactose fermenter and forms pale colonies on MacConkey.
questions.keyConcept: Watery diarrhea + rose-pink colonies on MacConkey agar (lactose fermenter) = ETEC (Enterotoxigenic E. coli).

media.caption: MacConkey agar showing rose-pink lactose-fermenting colonies

questions.text: In your lab, you received a stool sample from a patient complaining of watery diarrhea. Macroscopic appearance shows watery stool without blood or mucus. The causative organism was isolated on MacConkey agar (rose-pink colonies) and showed Gram-negative bacilli. If the organism is lactose fermenting, what is the next discriminatory step?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: When a lactose-fermenting Gram-negative rod is recovered from stool, performing the oxidase test is the essential first step to confirm membership in the family Enterobacteriaceae (which are oxidase-negative). This excludes oxidase-positive lactose-fermenting organisms such as Aeromonas hydrophila or Plesiomonas shigelloides.

Option B (Catalase) is ubiquitous among aerobic Gram-negative rods. Option C (Indole) is performed later as part of IMViC profiling. Option D (Hippurate hydrolysis) is used for Campylobacter jejuni or Group B Streptococcus.
questions.keyConcept: Oxidase test confirms Enterobacteriaceae status (oxidase-negative) and rules out oxidase-positive lookalikes (Aeromonas).

media.caption: MacConkey agar plate with pink colonies alongside Gram stain showing Gram-negative bacilli

questions.text: In your lab, you received a stool sample from a patient complaining of watery diarrhea. The causative organism was isolated as a lactose-fermenting Gram-negative rod on MacConkey agar. This organism (E. coli) will most likely be:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Escherichia coli displays the classic IMViC signature ++--:
1. Indole: POSITIVE (tryptophan converted to indole, forming a bright red ring with Kovac's reagent)
2. Methyl Red: POSITIVE (mixed acid fermentation)
3. Voges-Proskauer: NEGATIVE
4. Citrate: NEGATIVE (cannot use citrate as sole carbon source, medium remains green).
On TSI, E. coli ferments lactose, sucrose, and glucose, producing an acid slant / acid butt (A/A) with gas.

Option A is incorrect because E. coli is urease-negative (unlike Proteus). Option B is incorrect because E. coli is citrate-negative. Option D is incorrect because E. coli produces an acid (yellow) butt, not alkaline.
questions.keyConcept: E. coli biochemical profile: Indole positive, Methyl red positive, VP negative, Citrate negative (IMViC ++--), TSI A/A with gas.

media.caption: Lactose-fermenting colonies of E. coli on MacConkey agar

questions.text: Four hours after consuming potato and rice meals at a restaurant, 5 friends developed severe nausea and projectile vomiting. Remnants of the food were tested. Direct microscopy revealed Gram-positive cocci in clusters, catalase-positive. Culture showed beta-hemolytic colonies on blood agar and yellow colonies on Mannitol Salt Agar (MSA). What is your provisional diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Staphylococcal food poisoning has a rapid onset (1 to 6 hours, characteristically ~4 hours) mediated by preformed heat-stable enterotoxin (Enterotoxins A–E). Symptoms are dominated by violent vomiting, nausea, and abdominal cramps without fever. Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive coccus in grape-like clusters, catalase-positive, coagulase-positive, produces beta-hemolysis on blood agar, and ferments mannitol on MSA turning the medium yellow.

Option A and B (ETEC, EHEC) are Gram-negative bacilli with incubation periods of 1–3 days. Option D (Vibrio cholerae) has an incubation period of 1–3 days and causes painless rice-water diarrhea.
questions.keyConcept: Rapid food poisoning (1–6 hrs, vomiting) + Gram-positive cocci in clusters + golden yellow colonies on MSA = Staph. aureus.

media.caption: Staph. aureus: Beta-hemolysis on blood agar and mannitol-fermenting yellow colonies on MSA

questions.text: Four hours after consuming potatoes and rice meals in a restaurant, 5 friends developed symptoms of food poisoning. S. aureus was isolated from the food remnants. The following test grid was set up to trace the source of infection among kitchen workers. How can you trace the source of infection?
options: Agglutination tests to detect O antigens
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Bacteriophage typing (phage typing) is the classical epidemiological tool for Staphylococcus aureus. A standardized grid of specific staphylococcal bacteriophages (Groups I, II, III, IV) is applied to an agar lawn inoculated with the isolate. Lytic plaques identify the precise phage pattern of the strain, matching food isolates to the asymptomatic carrier (e.g., food handler's nasal or skin carriage).

Option A (Colicin typing) is for Shigella. Option C (Widal test) is for enteric fever. Option D (O antigens) is for Gram-negative enteric rods.
questions.keyConcept: Bacteriophage typing (phage typing) is the definitive epidemiological method for tracing Staphylococcus aureus outbreaks.

media.caption: Phage typing grid showing specific lytic plaque patterns for Staph. aureus

questions.text: Staphylococcus aureus cultured on Mannitol Salt Agar (MSA) produces which characteristic appearance?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Mannitol Salt Agar contains 7.5% NaCl (which inhibits non-staphylococci), mannitol (carbohydrate), and phenol red (pH indicator). Staphylococcus aureus actively ferments mannitol, generating acids that lower the pH and shift phenol red from red to bright yellow, yielding yellow colonies surrounded by bright yellow zones.

Option A and C are incorrect because S. aureus ferments mannitol. Option B is incorrect because mannitol fermentation produces yellow, not clear colonies (Staphylococcus epidermidis produces clear colonies with red medium).
questions.keyConcept: Staph. aureus on MSA: Halotolerant, ferments mannitol, turning phenol red from red to yellow.

media.caption: Mannitol Salt Agar: Yellow coloration confirms mannitol fermentation by S. aureus

questions.text: A 15-year-old girl presented with high stepladder fever, abdominal pain, and constipation for 7 days. Your preliminary diagnosis for this case is enteric fever (typhoid fever). The most appropriate diagnostic specimen at this stage (Day 7 / 1st week) would be:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: In enteric fever (Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi/Paratyphi), the primary diagnostic specimen correlates with disease chronometry:
- 1st week: Blood culture has the highest diagnostic yield (80–90% positive) because primary bacteremia is occurring.
- 2nd–3rd week: Stool and urine culture yield rises as organisms are shed into the biliary tract and urine.
- Late 2nd–3rd week: Serum for Widal serological test reaches diagnostic titer.
At Day 7, a blood sample for culture is the gold standard.
questions.keyConcept: Enteric fever chronometry: 1st week = Blood culture (80–90% sensitivity); 2nd–3rd week = Stool/Urine culture; 3rd week = Serum (Widal).

questions.text: A 15-year-old girl presented with fever, abdominal pain, and constipation for 7 days. Isolation of the blood culture isolate revealed: TSI showing alkaline slant / acid butt (K/A) with abundant gas and black H2S precipitate, Indole negative, Urease negative, and Simmon's Citrate POSITIVE (tube turned royal blue). The causative agent is most likely:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Salmonella paratyphi B (Salmonella enterica serovar Paratyphi B / Schottmülleri) is distinguished biochemically by:
1. TSI: Alkaline slant / acid butt (K/A) with abundant gas and heavy black H2S production.
2. Citrate: POSITIVE (Simmons citrate agar turns from green to royal blue due to alkaline pH from citrate utilization).
3. Indole: Negative.
4. Urease: Negative.

Option A (S. paratyphi A) is citrate-negative, H2S-negative, and produces gas. Option D (S. typhi) is citrate-NEGATIVE, produces NO gas, and produces only a modest trace ring of H2S. Option C (Shigella) produces no H2S, no gas, and is citrate-negative.
questions.keyConcept: Salmonella paratyphi B: TSI K/A + gas + heavy H2S, and strictly Citrate POSITIVE (blue tube).

media.caption: Biochemical reactions: TSI K/A + gas + H2S, Indole negative, Urease negative, Citrate positive (blue)

questions.text: A 15-year-old girl presented with fever, abdominal pain, and constipation for 7 days. Isolation was done and revealed: TSI showing alkaline slant / acid butt (K/A) with a faint black ring of H2S at the slant/butt junction, NO gas, Indole negative, Urease negative, and Citrate NEGATIVE (medium remains green). The causative agent is most likely:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Salmonella typhi possesses a unique biochemical fingerprint:
1. TSI: Alkaline slant / acid butt (K/A) with only a faint/trace black ring of H2S at the junction, and complete ABSENCE of gas production (anaerogenic glucose fermentation).
2. Simmons Citrate: NEGATIVE (medium remains green).
3. Indole: Negative.
4. Urease: Negative.

Option B (S. paratyphi B) produces abundant gas, heavy H2S, and is citrate-positive (blue). Option A (S. paratyphi A) produces gas and no H2S. Option C (Shigella) produces no H2S at all.
questions.keyConcept: Salmonella typhi: TSI K/A, trace H2S ring, NO gas, Indole negative, Urease negative, Citrate NEGATIVE (green tube).

media.caption: Biochemical panel of S. typhi: TSI K/A with trace H2S and no gas, Citrate negative (green)

questions.text: A 15-year-old girl presented with fever, abdominal pain, and constipation for 12 days. Your preliminary diagnosis for this case is enteric fever. The appropriate specimen for isolation at this stage (Day 12 / 2nd week) would be:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: By the second week (Days 8–14) of typhoid fever, Salmonella bacilli reach the liver via the bloodstream, multiply in the gallbladder and Peyer's patches, and are heavily excreted into the intestinal lumen via bile. Consequently, stool culture positivity increases significantly (yielding 70–80% positive isolates in the 2nd and 3rd weeks).

Option A (Blood) has declining sensitivity by Day 12 compared to week 1. Option B (Anal swab) is inadequate for culture yield. Option C (Serum) is for serological antibody testing (Widal), not organism isolation.
questions.keyConcept: In the 2nd and 3rd weeks of enteric fever, stool culture yield rises dramatically as bacteria are excreted from the gallbladder into feces.

questions.text: A 15-year-old girl presented with fever, abdominal pain, and constipation for 3 weeks. Your preliminary diagnosis for this case is enteric fever. The appropriate sample(s) for diagnostic testing would be:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: In the 3rd week of enteric fever, two complementary diagnostic approaches are appropriate:
1. Serum sample: For the Widal agglutination test, as circulating anti-O and anti-H agglutinins reach peak diagnostic titers.
2. Stool sample: For culture, as biliary shedding remains maximal.
Therefore, both Serum (C) and Stool (D) are appropriate diagnostic specimens.
questions.keyConcept: 3rd week of enteric fever: Serum (peak Widal antibody titer) and Stool (persistent excretion) are the optimal diagnostic samples.

questions.text: A 15-year-old girl presented with fever, abdominal pain, and constipation for 12 days. Enteric fever is suspected. After collection of the stool specimen, primary inoculation and enrichment should be done FIRST on:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Stool contains millions of commensal bacteria (E. coli, enterococci, Proteus) per gram. Inoculating stool directly onto solid agar risks overgrowing Salmonella. Selenite F broth (or tetrathionate broth) is an enrichment fluid medium containing sodium selenite, which selectively inhibits commensal coliforms during the first 12–18 hours of incubation, allowing Salmonella to multiply rapidly before subculture onto solid selective media.

Option A and C are solid plating media used after enrichment. Option B (Blood agar) is non-selective.
questions.keyConcept: Fecal isolation of Salmonella begins with enrichment in Selenite F broth to suppress coliform overgrowth.

media.caption: Enrichment protocol: Selenite broth tube followed by subculture on DCA / SS agar

questions.text: A 15-year-old girl presented with fever, abdominal pain, and constipation for 12 days. Enteric fever is suspected. After enrichment of the stool specimen in selenite broth, the proper selective differential solid medium for plating and isolation of Salmonella is:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Deoxycholate Citrate Agar (DCA) and Salmonella-Shigella (SS) agar are highly selective and differential media for Salmonella. Sodium deoxycholate and citrate inhibit Gram-positive bacteria and most coliforms. Salmonella does not ferment lactose (forming pale, translucent colonies) and produces H2S from sodium thiosulfate, which reacts with ferric citrate to produce characteristic black centers.

Option B (Blood agar) is non-selective. Option C (MacConkey) is only moderately selective. Option D (TCBS) is selective for Vibrio cholerae.
questions.keyConcept: DCA and SS agar: Selective for Salmonella, producing pale (non-lactose fermenting) colonies with black centers (H2S positive).

media.caption: Selenite broth followed by plating onto DCA/SS agar

questions.text: You are provided with the following qualitative Widal slide agglutination test showing visible granular agglutination with O antigen and floccular agglutination with H antigen, while AH and BH show no clumping. Negative control (NC) is clear and positive control (PC) is clumped. What is your interpretation?
options: No need to perform a quantitative test
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: The slide shows distinct clumping in both the Somatic O well (compact granular agglutination) and the Flagellar H well (loose floccular agglutination) of Salmonella typhi, with no agglutination in the Paratyphi A (AH) or Paratyphi B (BH) wells. Therefore, the screening test is positive for both O and H antigens of S. typhi, requiring a quantitative tube agglutination test to determine diagnostic titers.

Option A is incorrect because clumping is clearly present. Option C is incorrect because H is also positive. Option D is incorrect because a positive qualitative slide must always be followed by quantitative tube titration.
questions.keyConcept: Qualitative Widal: Clumping with both O and H antigens indicates presumptive positive S. typhi reaction, mandating quantitative titration.

media.caption: Qualitative Widal slide agglutination test: Clumping in O and H wells, clear in AH and BH

questions.text: You are provided with the following quantitative Widal tube agglutination rack. The highest serum dilution showing visible agglutination (indicated by the arrow) is the 4th tube (1/160), with clearing of supernatant. What is the antibody titer?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: In a quantitative Widal tube agglutination test, doubling serial dilutions of patient serum are prepared (1/20, 1/40, 1/80, 1/160, 1/320...). The antibody titer is defined as the reciprocal of the highest dilution of serum that produces visible agglutination (clumping of bacteria with clearing of the supernatant). Here, agglutination is evident up to tube 4 (1/160), establishing a titer of 1/160 (clinically significant in endemic areas).

Options A, B, and C are lower dilutions that showed clumping, but the titer is defined by the endpoint (highest dilution).
questions.keyConcept: Widal titer is the highest serum dilution demonstrating visible agglutination (here, 1/160).

media.caption: Quantitative Widal tube agglutination test indicating an endpoint titer of 1/160

questions.text: You are provided with a quantitative Widal test. Which of the following type-specific antigens is used to differentiate specific serotypes of Salmonella (e.g. Typhi vs. Paratyphi A vs. Paratyphi B)?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Salmonella antigenic structure comprises:
- Somatic O antigen (lipopolysaccharide): Group-specific (defines serogroups A, B, C, D).
- Flagellar H antigen (protein): Type-specific (defines individual serotypes within a group, e.g. H-d for S. typhi, H-a for S. paratyphi A, H-b for S. paratyphi B).
- Vi antigen: Capsular polysaccharide found in S. typhi.
Therefore, the Flagellar H antigen is the type-specific antigen that differentiates Salmonella serotypes.

Option A (Somatic O) is group-specific. Option C and D are not used to differentiate serotypes in the Widal panel.
questions.keyConcept: In Salmonella serology: Somatic O is group-specific; Flagellar H is type-specific.

media.caption: Widal tube rack demonstrating separate testing of O, H, HA, and HB antigens
